sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Procedural Lacunae**: The EIA process often suffers from **Post-facto clearance**, where projects operate without prior approval, violating the 'Precautionary Principle'.
• **Institutional Weakness**: The **Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC)** and **State Level EAC (SEAC)** often lack multidisciplinary expertise, leading to superficial scrutiny.
• **Public Participation Deficit**: Public hearings are frequently reduced to a **'Check-box exercise'** rather than a genuine consultative process, often marred by intimidation or lack of information transparency.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **'Quality of EIA Reports'** is the primary bottleneck, as consultants are hired by project proponents, creating a **Conflict of Interest**.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Lack of independent monitoring bodies; reliance on project proponent data.
Regulatory capture and understaffing of State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs).
Exemption of strategic projects; dilution of public hearing norms.
EIA Notification 2020 draft controversies and 'Ease of Doing Business' pressure.

items.definition: Granting environmental clearance to projects that have already commenced construction without prior approval, effectively bypassing the precautionary principle.
A situation where the regulatory agency (MoEFCC/SEIAA) acts in the interest of the industry it is supposed to regulate rather than the public interest.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **PARIVESH Portal**: Single-window integrated environmental management system to track clearance status.
• **EIA Notification 2006**: The primary legal framework governing the categorization of projects (Category A and B).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of cumulative impact assessment; poor post-clearance monitoring.
• **Solutions**: Establishing an independent National Environmental Regulator (NER) as suggested by the Supreme Court in the Lafarge Umiam Mining case.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: **'P-I-C-K'** (Drawbacks of EIA).
• **Decoded Meaning**: **P**ost-facto clearance, **I**nstitutional weakness, **C**onflict of interest (consultants), **K**nowledge/Data gaps.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames questions implying that EIA is a 'statutory' requirement under the Constitution. It is NOT; it is statutory under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Environmental Rule of Law' and cite the 'Lafarge Umiam Mining Pvt. Ltd. vs. Union of India' case to emphasize the need for an independent regulator.

keyTakeaways: EIA is a tool for sustainable development, not a hurdle to economic growth.
The primary drawback is the lack of independence in the appraisal process.
Post-clearance monitoring is the weakest link in the current Indian EIA regime.
